Additionally, the site plan does not show clearance dimension callouts demonstrating 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor for any items that may be placed at the easement edge. findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows mitigation trees ('M' designation) and other plantings near the overhead electric line shown along the southern boundary of the site. Tree list (Sheet 32) provides caliper sizes and species. However, no lateral distance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan indicating how far proposed trees are located from the overhead electric conductors. Per UCM § 1.10.10.4, trees must maintain 50 lateral feet from transmission conductors (or 10 lateral feet from distribution conductors if facility is distribution rather than transmission). Tree species must be verified against ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation for trees within the clearance zones. Applicant must provide: (1) dimension callouts showing lateral distances from OHE to all trees within 50 feet of the line; (2) confirmation that tree species are from the UC list; (3) site grading contours showing clearance compliance.
applicableAreas: Trees near overhead electric transmission lines

Live Oak is not utility-compatible (mature height 60+ feet exceeds UC list criteria); Cedar Elm (mature height 40-60 feet) is problematic near distribution lines. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution lines must be from ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible list with mature heights ≤20 feet generally.
applicableAreas: Landscape plantings within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of overhead transmission conductors

findings.comment: Root barrier specifications are not visible on landscape plan or landscape details (Sheet 37). The root barrier requirement applies only when trees are within 20 feet of underground equipment, which cannot be determined from available documentation due to lack of cross-reference between tree and equipment locations. No root barrier details or specifications are noted on the landscape plan for any trees near utilities.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment

findings.comment: Root barrier requirements apply only if trees are proposed within 20 feet of underground equipment (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment). The landscape plan does not provide dimensional analysis of tree locations relative to underground equipment, so applicability cannot be determined. Additionally, no root barrier details or specifications are provided on the landscape plan or landscape details sheets. Cannot verify whether this requirement applies or, if it does, whether it is satisfied.

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows trees near overhead electric distribution line with symbols labeled only as 'M' (mitigation tree) and other abbreviations (SY, PL, P), but does not include a legend identifying the specific species names for trees shown in areas with utility facilities. Plant species identification requires reference to separate Sheet 35, which is not cross-referenced on the landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan area near overhead electric facilities (southern boundary OHE line)

findings.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree symbols labeled only by functional category ('M' for mitigation tree, 'SY' for street yard tree, 'PL' for parking lot tree, 'P' for parking buffer point tree). These abbreviations indicate regulatory category, not species identification. Tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) are identified only on a separate landscape calculations sheet (Sheet 35), not on the landscape plan itself. A user reading the landscape plan cannot identify which specific tree species is shown at each location without cross-referencing to another sheet. The plant legend on the landscape plan does not include species identification.
applicableAreas: entire landscape plan, particularly trees near utility facilities

findings.comment: If transformer pads are proposed with clearances less than 5 feet to buildings, applicant must provide: (1) written Austin Energy Design approval, (2) architectural specifications confirming 3-hour fire rating in clearance areas, (3) verification that location does not face confined space, (4) confirmation of 10+ feet clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (5) verification of 15+ feet vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are labeled on plans, so it cannot be determined whether reduced 3-foot clearances are shown. If reduced clearances exist, the required documentation (AE Design written approval, fire rating verification, confined space confirmation, vertical clearance to windows/doors) is not provided on the plans.

findings.comment: Building floor plans showing fire exit stairwell locations are not provided in the site plan submittal. Applicant must provide building floor plans identifying exit stair locations and dimension callouts confirming adequate clearance from transformer pads to all fire exit stairs.

findings.comment: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains a note stating that a pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction (Electric Transmission Notes, Item 3). However, this is a transmission-specific note. The required standard note for all projects with overhead high-voltage lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, stating that the owner/contractor must NOTIFY Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines, is not present in a standard location (cover sheet or general notes) in the standard required format. The current note references a safety meeting but does not include the explicit 48-hour notification requirement language mandated by Texas law.
applicableAreas: Cover sheets and general notes
